problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a globally differentiable, L-smooth objective F that may be nonconvex. A global minimizer xstar satisfies ‖xstar−x0‖≤R. Convexity of F itself and strong convexity are not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LocalHiddenConvexStochastic.lean: spec.admissible, gradient smoothness and global-minimizer clauses.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Local hidden convexity: F=H∘c on ball(x0,3R), where H is convex and differentiable on an open convex set U. For x∈closedBall(x0,2R), c(x)∈U and Dc(x)=J(x).
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LocalHiddenConvexStochastic.lean: Instance and spec.admissible, composition, ConvexOn, DifferentiableAt, and HasFDerivAt clauses.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query x returns g(x,ξ)∈E with Eξ[g(x,ξ)]=∇F(x) and Eξ‖g(x,ξ)−∇F(x)‖²≤σ² for every x. Fresh seeds are independent with a common probability law. The oracle supplies gradients only; function values, c, H, and J are unavailable. The supplied budget counts individual oracle replies and is a fixed call cap.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LocalHiddenConvexStochastic.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible oracle construction; LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean: StochasticGradient.IsStochasticGradient; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform variance bound σ²≥0 on the squared norm of the unbiased gradient error, with joint measurability and the stated integrability conditions. No almost-sure error bound, tail bound, or sample-gradient smoothness is assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean: StochasticGradient.IsStochasticGradient.measurable, integrable, unbiased, variance_integrable, and variance; LongTails/Setups/LocalHiddenConvexStochastic.lean: spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure and second-countable topology. No dimension bound is supplied.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LocalHiddenConvexStochastic.lean: Public.finiteE, Public.linearE, Public.completeE, Public.borelE, and Public.countableE.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The hidden Jacobian satisfies ‖J(x)v‖≥μ‖v‖ and ‖J(x)−J(y)‖≤LJ‖x−y‖ on closedBall(x0,2R), with μ>0, LJ≥0, and 32LJ R≤μ. Public information includes L>0, R>0, σ≥0, and x0. The structural parameters μ,LJ and target ε>0 are hidden from the algorithm constructor; ε can determine the execution budget.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LocalHiddenConvexStochastic.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible Jacobian clauses; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm and execute.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable E-valued point X with integrable objective gap F(X)−F(xstar), where xstar is a global minimizer. No feasibility region or particular iterate is imposed on the output.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[F(X)−F(xstar)]≤ε, with expectation over the joint algorithm and oracle randomness. No high-probability or almost-sure accuracy guarantee is required.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LocalHiddenConvexStochastic.lean: spec.successful integral inequality; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence product probability law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation combines stochastic gradient access with a hidden convex representation available only locally, quantitative control of its Jacobian variation, and structural parameters withheld from the algorithm.

descriptionHtml:
Local Hidden Convex Stochastic Minimization

We minimize a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function F:E→R on a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, with L>0, and a given point x0∈E is within distance R>0 of a global minimizer x⋆. Locally, F is a convex function composed with a differentiable change of coordinates whose derivative is uniformly nonsingular and varies slowly. The oracle returns unbiased stochastic gradients with variance at most σ2, where σ≥0, using independent samples. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable gap and E[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, averaging over oracle and independent algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈EF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. Write B(x,r) and B―(x,r) for the open and closed balls. The algorithm receives only E, the measurable sample space Ω, L, R, σ, and x0; the parameters μ>0, LJ≥0, and ε>0 may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Local hidden convexity). There exist functions H:E→R and c:E→E, an open convex set U⊆E, and a map J assigning a linear operator J(x):E→E to each x∈E, such that F(x)=H(c(x)),x∈B(x0,3R). The function H is differentiable on U and satisfies H((1−t)u+tv)≤(1−t)H(u)+tH(v),u,v∈U,t∈[0,1]. For every x∈B―(x0,2R), we have c(x)∈U, the map c is Fréchet differentiable at x with derivative J(x), and μ∥v∥≤∥J(x)v∥,v∈E. The derivative satisfies ∥J(x)−J(y)∥op≤LJ∥x−y∥,x,y∈B―(x0,2R),32LJR≤μ.

Assumption 2 (Global smoothness). The function F is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and ∥∇F(x)−∇F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 4 (Stochastic gradient oracle). Let ν be a probability measure on Ω. The oracle is a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the random vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,ξ)−∇F(x)∥2 is integrable for ξ∼ν, with Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇F(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇F(x)∥2]≤σ2. At the kth query x, the oracle returns g(x,ξk), where (ξk)k≥0 are independent with common law ν and are independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

Queries may be made at any point of E. Let P be the joint law of the oracle samples and the algorithm’s randomness. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable under P, and it must satisfy EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
In a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, F is globally L-smooth and has a global minimizer x⋆∈B―(x0,R). On B(x0,3R), F=H∘c, with H convex and differentiable on an open convex set U. On B―(x0,2R), c(x)∈U, Dc(x)=J(x), ∥J(x)v∥≥μ∥v∥, and J is LJ-Lipschitz; 32LJR≤μ. Here L,R,μ,ε>0 and LJ,σ≥0. IID samples have law p; the jointly measurable oracle g satisfies ∫g(x,ω)dp=∇F(x) and ∫∥g(x,ω)−∇F(x)∥2dp≤σ2, with the required integrability. Target: ∫[F(xK)−F(x⋆)]dP≤ε, P=p⊗N. Result (1) constructs safeguarded similar triangles, using L,R,σ,x0; stopping also needs ε.

Local hidden-convex stochastic optimization: LocalHiddenConvexStochastic.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) HiddenConvexAcceleratedStochastic (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+(LR2ε+σ2R2ε2)ℓ2) stochastic-gradient calls.
(2) Momentum P-SGD (Fatkhullin et al. 2024, Thm. 8) O((1+Ld2ε+Ld4σ2ε3)ℓ0) calls, including initialization. Restriction: compact convex X∋x0,x⋆, convex c(X), and c−1 is 1/μc-Lipschitz; d=DU/μc. (1): On the overlap d≍R, ε−1→ε−1/2 and LR4σ2/ε3→σ2R2/ε2, up to logarithms; total gain for fixed parameters and sufficiently small ε. Scope: no compact convex image required. Adaptivity: updates need neither ε,DU,μc; stopping needs ε. (1) adds local C1,1 regularity and 32LJR≤μ; requires an unconstrained global minimizer. Classes are incomparable.
(3) (Bhaskara et al. 2025, Thm. 5.4) O(1+D2ρ+D24G3ρ(αβ)4ε3) calls. Restriction: global invertible c, ∥J∥≤1/α, ∥J−1∥≤1/β, ρ-Lipschitz J; G-Lipschitz H, ∥g∥≤G a.s.; known radii D1,D2 with the radial level-set ordering of (A3). (1): On the smooth overlap, fixed positive parameters and ε↓0, ε−3→ε−2ℓ2. Scope: bounded variance replaces bounded gradients; local replaces global Jacobian regularity. Full parameter bounds are not comparable. (1) requires global L-smoothness and 32LJR≤μ; loses nonsmooth objectives and the unrestricted global regime.
(4) AC-SA (Lan 2012, Cor. 1) O(1+LR2ε+σ2R2ε2) calls. Special case: LJ=0, with optimization restricted to B―(x0,R), where F is convex. (1): Scope extends convex optimization to locally near-affine hidden convexity, including nonconvex, non-quasar-convex objectives. (1) loses a factor ℓ2 on the convex overlap.

Abbr: L: gradient Lipschitz constant; R: initial-distance bound; σ2: variance bound; ε: expected objective-gap target; μ: least singular-value bound for J; LJ: Jacobian Lipschitz constant; ℓ=log⁡(2+LR2/ε+σ2R2/ε2). In (2), DU=diam(c(X)), d=DU/μc, and ℓ0=log⁡(2+(LR2+σ2/L)/ε) for one-sample gradient initialization. In (3), G denotes the paper’s bound H, ρ its Jacobian Lipschitz constant, α,β its distortion parameters, and D1,D2 its radial bounds about x0; radial ordering means F(y)≥F(x) whenever ∥x−x0∥=D1, ∥y−x0∥=D2.

Bhaskara, Aditya, Ashok Cutkosky, Ravi Kumar, and Manish Purohit. 2025. “Descent with Misaligned Gradients and Applications to Hidden Convexity.” International Conference on Learning Representations. https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/c40fc068ed2b4ad43bff4f3f3206691e-Abstract-Conference.html.
Fatkhullin, Ilyas, Niao He, and Yifan Hu. 2024. Stochastic Optimization Under Hidden Convexity. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2401.00108.
Lan, Guanghui. 2012. “An Optimal Method for Stochastic Composite Optimization.” Mathematical Programming 133 (1–2): 365–97. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-010-0434-y.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

open MeasureTheory Metric

namespace LongTails.Setups.LocalHiddenConvexStochastic

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.finiteE Public.completeE
  Public.measurableE Public.borelE Public.countableE Public.measurableΩ

structure Params extends Public where
  μ : ℝ
  LJ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  F : p.E → ℝ
  H : p.E → ℝ
  c : p.E → p.E
  J : p.E → p.E →L[ℝ] p.E
  U : Set p.E

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 < q.μ ∧ 0 ≤ q.LJ ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧
    32 * q.LJ * q.R ≤ q.μ
  admissible q I O :=
    ∃ (oracle : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω),
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := ⟨Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => (p : Measure q.Ω)), inferInstance⟩
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => oracle x seed } ∧
    (∀ x ∈ ball q.x0 (3 * q.R), I.F x = I.H (I.c x)) ∧
    IsOpen I.U ∧ ConvexOn ℝ I.U I.H ∧ (∀ u ∈ I.U, DifferentiableAt ℝ I.H u) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ closedBall q.x0 (2 * q.R), I.c x ∈ I.U ∧ HasFDerivAt I.c (I.J x) x ∧
      ∀ v, q.μ * ‖v‖ ≤ ‖I.J x v‖) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ closedBall q.x0 (2 * q.R), ∀ y ∈ closedBall q.x0 (2 * q.R),
      ‖I.J x - I.J y‖ ≤ q.LJ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt I.F (gradient I.F x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient I.F x - gradient I.F y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ closedBall q.x0 q.R, IsMinOn I.F Set.univ xstar) ∧
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex.IsStochasticGradient q.E q.Ω p I.F oracle q.σ
  successful q I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn I.F Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => I.F (output ω) - I.F xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, I.F (output ω) - I.F xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.LocalHiddenConvexStochastic
